div.div: مَقِيتٌ and ↓ مَمْقُوتٌ Hated: (S, K:) or the former signifies hateful, and the latter hated: (MF:) [or hateful, and hated, on account of his having committed a foul action: in this sense مقيت is mentioned by Lth: or hateful, and hated, in the utmost degree, on account of a foul action: in this sense مقيت is mentioned in the Msb.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
